mainTopic: בלעם's death, and the brilliance, downfall and punishment of דואג and אחיתופל
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of בלעם and then turns to דואג and אחיתופל, two great scholars who lost their share in עולם הבא. רב teaches that בלעם suffered all four court deaths. רבי חנינא works out from a פסוק that בלעם died at about 33, and a מין confirms this from בלעם's own notebook. מר בריה דרבינא teaches that we may expound freely only against בלעם. The גמרא then explains the two spellings of דואג's name. A string of רבי יצחק's teachings follows: they describe דואג's vast learning, which stayed only on his lips, and דוד's prayers that he lose everything. רבא teaches that asking many questions is not greatness, because הקב״ה wants the heart. The amud ends with how דואג died, how short the lives of דואג and אחיתופל were, and how דוד called אחיתופל first teacher, then colleague, then student. That last proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: בלעם received all four court deaths
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the פסוק saying בנ"י killed בלעם 'among their slain' means they carried out all four court deaths on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'The children of Israel killed [with the sword] among their slain.' רב said: this means they carried out on him all four kinds of death: stoning, burning, beheading, and strangling.
steps.whatsHappening: רב reads a פסוק about בלעם's death and teaches that he was put through all four deaths a בית דין can give.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק adds the strange words 'among their slain' instead of just saying they killed him. רב takes this extra wording to mean that בלעם's death included every type of killing: סקילה, שריפה, הרג, and חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: The four kinds of death penalty a בית דין can give

phrases.english: "The children of Israel killed [with the sword]
phrases.notes: יהושע 13:22. The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: among their slain"

four kinds of death:
stoning, and burning, beheading, and strangling.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'among their slain' teach that בלעם suffered all four court deaths.

steps.title: A heretic asks how old בלעם was
steps.stepSummary: A מין asks רבי חנינא whether he knows בלעם's age when he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain heretic said to רבי חנינא: Have you heard how old בלעם was?
steps.whatsHappening: A מין asks רבי חנינא a question about בלעם's age. This sets up the next step, where רבי חנינא answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה never gives בלעם's age directly. So the question tests whether the חכמים can figure it out from the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: A heretic (a person who rejects the תורה's teachings)
Have you heard? (did you get a tradition about this?)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: A certain heretic said to Rabbi Chanina:
Have you heard
how old Bilaam was?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ בִּלְעָם בַּר כַּמָּה הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about בלעם, the same person discussed in step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How old was בלעם when he died?

steps.title: רבי חנינא works out בלעם's age from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says the age is not written, but a פסוק in תהלים shows that wicked men do not live half their days, so בלעם was 33 or 34.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is not written outright. But since it is written, 'Men of blood and deceit will not live out half their days,' he was thirty-three or thirty-four years old.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the question by using a פסוק about wicked people dying young.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal lifespan is 70 years, so half would be 35. The פסוק says murderers and liars do not reach half their days. That means בלעם, who was both, died a bit before 35: at 33 or 34.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not written outright in the text
Men of blood and deceit (murderers and liars)
They will not live half their days

phrases.english: He said to him: It is not written outright,
but from the fact that it is written
"Men of blood and deceit
phrases.notes: תהלים 55:24

phrases.english: will not live out half their days,"
he was thirty-three years old
or thirty-four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בלעם was 33 or 34, based on the פסוק that wicked men do not live half their days.

steps.title: The heretic confirms the age from בלעם's notebook
steps.stepSummary: The מין agrees with רבי חנינא and says he saw בלעם's own record book, which says בלעם was 33 when פנחס killed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You have spoken well. I myself saw בלעם's notebook, and it was written in it: 'בלעם the lame was thirty-three years old when פנחס the robber killed him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The מין backs up רבי חנינא's answer with a written record he says he saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא's answer came only from a פסוק. Here an outside record matches it exactly at 33, which supports his reasoning. The notebook was written from בלעם's side, so it calls פנחס a robber.

keyTerms.meaning: You have spoken well (you are right)

phrases.english: He said to him: You have spoken well,
I myself have seen
the notebook of Bilaam,
and it was written in it:
Thirty-three years old
was Bilaam the lame
when Pinchas the robber killed him.
phrases.notes: The notebook's writer is on בלעם's side, so he insults פנחס by calling him a robber.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרַתְּ, לְדִידִי חֲזֵי לִי פִּנְקָסֵיהּ דְּבִלְעָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the answer given in step 3
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's conclusion that בלעם died at about 33
steps.raayaSupportSource: בלעם's own record book, which the מין says he saw
steps.whatToRemember: בלעם died young, at 33. רבי חנינא learned this from a פסוק, and the מין confirmed it from a written record.

steps.title: Expound freely only against בלעם
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבינא tells his son not to keep expounding against the others on the list, except for בלעם, against whom any hint may be expounded.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרבינא said to his son: With all of them, do not go too far in expounding, except for בלעם the wicked. Whatever you find about him, expound about him.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בריה דרבינא gives his son a rule about how far to go in expounding פסוקים against the people who lose their share in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the other people on the list, we should not hunt for extra דרשות that make them look bad. בלעם is different: he was so wicked that any hint against him in the פסוקים may be expounded.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא לִבְרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Mar the son of Ravina said to his son:
With all of them, do not go too far in expounding,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means everyone the משנה lists as having no share in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: except for Bilaam the wicked,
for whatever you find about him,
expound about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכוּלְּהוּ לָא תַּפֵּישׁ לְמִדְרַשׁ, לְבַר מִבִּלְעָם הָרָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a closing rule that explains why the גמרא has expounded so much against בלעם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not keep expounding against the others on the list, but any hint against בלעם may be expounded.
steps.whatToRemember: בלעם is the one exception: we may expound against him freely, but we hold back with the others.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the גמרא piles up so many דרשות against בלעם, and it teaches restraint when speaking about the others on the list.

steps.title: דואג's name is spelled two different ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the name דואג appears in one פסוק as דואג and in another as דויג.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'דואג,' and it is written 'דויג.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic, דואג, by pointing out that his name is spelled two different ways. This sets up רבי יוחנן's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same person's name should be spelled the same way. The change in spelling seems to carry a message, so the גמרא needs to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written one way, and it is written another way (two פסוקים that don't match)
דואג, a person in the days of שאול; the word also means 'worries'

phrases.english: It is written "Doeg,"
phrases.notes: שמואל א 22:9

phrases.english: and it is written "Doyeig."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 22:18

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves בלעם and opens a new topic about דואג
steps.kashyaTarget: The two different spellings of דואג's name in the פסוקים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One person's name should not be spelled two ways, so there must be a reason for the change.

steps.title: First God worried, then He cried 'woe'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains: 'דואג' hints that at first ה' worried this man would go bad, and 'דויג' hints that after he went bad, ה' said 'ווי' (woe).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: At first the Holy One, Blessed be He, sits and worries that perhaps this one will go out to an evil way. After he went out, He said: Woe, that this one went out!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the two spellings of the name: each one stands for a different stage in דואג's life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'דואג' sounds like 'worries,' which matches the time before he went bad, when ה' was worried about him. The added 'י' in 'דויג' hints at 'ווי' (woe), which matches the time after he actually went bad.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He (ה')

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: בַּתְּחִילָּה יוֹשֵׁב הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְדוֹאֵג,
phrases.english: At first the Holy One, Blessed be He, sits and worries
that perhaps this one will go out
to an evil way.
After he went out, He said:
Woe, that this one went out!
phrases.notes: The extra 'י' in דויג is the hint for 'ווי,' the cry of woe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בַּתְּחִילָּה יוֹשֵׁב הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְדוֹאֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the spelling problem raised in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each spelling describes a different time in דואג's life
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two spellings look like a mismatch with no meaning
steps.terutzMaskana: 'דואג' is the worry before he went bad, and 'דויג' is the 'woe' after he went bad.
steps.whatToRemember: The two spellings of דואג tell his story: first ה' worried about him, and after he went bad, ה' said 'woe.'

steps.title: A memory list for the coming teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a short list of key words to help remember the order of רבי יצחק's teachings that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory list: mighty, wicked, and righteous, riches, and counter.)
steps.whatsHappening: This line does not teach anything yet. The גמרא is setting up a string of teachings and gives a list of key words so we remember their order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word stands for one teaching of רבי יצחק that comes next. גבור is step 9, רשע is step 10, צדיק is step 12, חיל is step 13, and סופר is step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid: a list of key words for remembering a group of teachings
Riches or strength; key word for a later teaching
One who counts; key word for a later teaching

phrases.english: (Memory list: mighty, wicked,
phrases.notes: These are just key words. Each one points to a teaching coming up, so you can remember the order.

phrases.english: and righteous, riches, and counter.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the דואג/דויג name teaching to a new group of teachings about דואג from רבי יצחק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lists the key words of the next five teachings: גבור, רשע, צדיק, חיל, סופר.

steps.title: Why would someone mighty in תורה boast of evil?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reads a פסוק in תהלים as הקב״ה scolding דואג: you are great in תורה and God's kindness is on you, so why boast about evil?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: What does the פסוק mean, 'Why do you boast of evil, mighty one? The kindness of God lasts all day'? הקב״ה said to דואג: Aren't you mighty in תורה? Why do you boast of evil? Isn't God's kindness spread over you all day?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק explains a פסוק in תהלים as words הקב״ה says to דואג. This is the first key word on the list, 'mighty.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק reads 'הגבור' (mighty one) as 'mighty in תורה,' not as physical strength. The second half of the פסוק, about God's kindness, becomes part of the scolding: you have God's kindness, so why choose evil?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? Opens an explanation of a פסוק
Mighty in תורה; a great scholar

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Why do you boast of evil, mighty one?
The kindness of God is all day long"?
phrases.notes: תהלים 52:3

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְדוֹאֵג:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Doeg:
Aren't you mighty in Torah?
Why do you boast of evil?

phrases.aramaic: לֹא חֶסֶד אֵל נָטוּי עָלֶיךָ כׇּל הַיּוֹם?
phrases.english: Isn't the kindness of God spread over you all day long?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First teaching on the memory list (גבור).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'הגבור' in the פסוק means דואג, who was mighty in תורה, and הקב״ה rebukes him for boasting of evil despite the kindness given to him.

steps.title: How can דואג teach laws he himself breaks?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reads another פסוק as הקב״ה asking דואג the wicked how he can teach the parts of the תורה about murderers and slanderers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: What does the פסוק mean, 'To the wicked one God said: What business do you have telling My laws?' הקב״ה said to דואג the wicked: What business do you have telling My laws? When you reach the section about murderers and the section about people who speak לשון הרע, how do you explain them?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second key word on the list, 'wicked.' רבי יצחק says the 'wicked one' in this פסוק is דואג, and הקב״ה questions his right to teach תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that a teacher who breaks the very laws he teaches has no business teaching them. הקב״ה picks murder and לשון הרע because those are the sins tied to דואג.

keyTerms.meaning: To tell or teach My laws
The section of the תורה about murderers
Explains or teaches a section of the תורה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"And to the wicked one God said:
What business do you have telling My laws"?
phrases.notes: תהלים 50:16

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְדוֹאֵג הָרָשָׁע:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Doeg the wicked:
What business do you have telling My laws?
When you reach the section about murderers
and the section about those who speak slander,
how do you explain them?
phrases.notes: He means: you did these very things yourself, so how can you stand up and teach them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second teaching on the memory list (רשע), following the first teaching about גבור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'רשע' in the פסוק is דואג, and הקב״ה challenges how he can teach laws about murder and slander that he himself broke.

steps.title: דואג's תורה was only on his lips
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the end of the same פסוק, and רבי אמי explains that דואג's תורה stayed in his mouth and never went deeper.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And you carried My covenant on your mouth.' רבי אמי said: דואג's תורה was only from the lip and outward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the second half of the same פסוק. רבי אמי uses the words 'on your mouth' to describe what kind of תורה דואג had.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the covenant was 'on your mouth,' not in your heart. רבי אמי reads this to mean דואג's learning was only outside talk, which explains how a great scholar could still act so badly.

keyTerms.meaning: From the lip and outward; only talk, not from the heart

steps.whatToRemember: דואג was great in תורה, but his learning was only on his lips. That is why he could teach laws he himself broke.

phrases.english: "And you carried My covenant on your mouth."
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק, תהלים 50:16.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
The Torah of Doeg is nothing
but from the lip and outward.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וַתִּשָּׂא בְרִיתִי עֲלֵי פִיךָ״. אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק from step 10, now its second half, through רבי אמי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דואג's תורה was only lip service, not from the heart.

steps.title: First the righteous feared him, then they laughed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains a פסוק to mean that the righteous first feared דואג, and in the end laughed at him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: What does the פסוק mean, 'The righteous will see and fear, and laugh at him'? At first they will fear, and in the end they will laugh.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third key word on the list, 'righteous.' רבי יצחק explains why the פסוק says the righteous both fear and laugh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fearing and laughing seem to clash, so רבי יצחק says they happen at two different times. First the righteous feared דואג, and later, when he fell, they laughed at him.

keyTerms.meaning: They will see / they will fear; two similar-looking words in the פסוק

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"And the righteous will see, and will fear,
phrases.notes: Watch the two words: וְיִרְאוּ means 'see' and וְיִירָאוּ means 'fear.'

phrases.english: and at him they will laugh"?
phrases.notes: תהלים 52:8

phrases.english: At first they will fear,
and in the end they will laugh.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״וְיִרְאוּ צַדִּיקִים וְיִירָאוּ וְעָלָיו יִשְׂחָקוּ״

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fear and laughter in the פסוק happen at different times: first the righteous fear דואג, and in the end they laugh at his downfall.

steps.title: דוד asks that דואג die
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reads a פסוק in איוב as a conversation. דוד asks that דואג die. הקב״ה says דואג will lose his 'wealth' on his own, and דוד answers that God should take it out of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: What does the פסוק 'He swallowed wealth and will vomit it out; God will cast it out of his belly' mean? דוד said to הקב״ה: Master of the world, let דואג die! God answered: 'He swallowed wealth and will vomit it out.' דוד replied: 'God will cast it out of his belly!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק splits one פסוק into two lines of a conversation between דוד and הקב״ה about דואג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק becomes God's answer: there is no need to kill דואג, because what he 'swallowed' will come out by itself. The second half becomes דוד's reply: let God Himself take it out of him now. The 'wealth' here is understood as דואג's תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: wealth, riches (here read as דואג's תורה)
and he will vomit it out
will drive it out, remove it

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"He swallowed wealth and will vomit it out;
God will cast it out of his belly"?
phrases.notes: איוב 20:15

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר דָּוִד לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: David said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world, let Doeg die!
He said to him: "He swallowed wealth and will vomit it out."
phrases.notes: God's point: דואג is full of תורה, but he will lose it on his own, so there is no need to kill him.

phrases.english: He said before Him: "God will cast it out of his belly!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth teaching on the memory list (חיל), after גבור, רשע and צדיק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק in איוב is read as a conversation: God says דואג will lose his תורה by himself, and דוד asks that God take it from him.

steps.title: No עולם הבא for דואג
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה suggests letting דואג into עולם הבא, and דוד answers with the פסוק 'God will destroy you forever.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: What does 'God will likewise destroy you forever' mean? הקב״ה said to דוד: Let דואג come into עולם הבא. דוד answered: 'God will likewise destroy you forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק reads a פסוק in תהלים as דוד's refusal when God suggests giving דואג a place in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'forever' (לָנֶצַח) is the key. דוד is not asking only for death in this world. He asks that דואג lose eternal life as well.

keyTerms.meaning: will tear you down, destroy you

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
What is the meaning of what is written: "God will likewise destroy you forever"?
phrases.notes: תהלים 52:7

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to David:
Let Doeg come into the World to Come.
He said before Him: "God will likewise destroy you forever."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״גַּם אֵל יִתׇּצְךָ לָנֶצַח״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same dialogue pattern between דוד and הקב״ה about דואג.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד, using the פסוק, refuses God's suggestion to give דואג a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: No teaching in his name and no scholar sons
steps.stepSummary: Using the rest of the same פסוק, הקב״ה makes two smaller offers. First, that a teaching be said in דואג's name. Second, that he have sons who are scholars. דוד turns down both with words from the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'He will break you and pluck you from the tent, and uproot you from the land of the living, Selah' mean? הקב״ה said: Let them say a teaching in the בית מדרש in his name. דוד answered: 'He will break you and pluck you from the tent.' God said: Let him have sons who are רבנן. דוד answered: 'And uproot you from the land of the living, Selah.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the same פסוק in תהלים as a back-and-forth. Each time, God offers דואג a smaller good thing, and דוד turns it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each offer is smaller than the one before: first עולם הבא, then a teaching quoted in his name, then sons who learn תורה. דוד answers with 'pluck you from the tent,' meaning keep him out of the tent of תורה. Then he answers with 'uproot you,' meaning leave him no roots at all, not even children who learn.

keyTerms.meaning: He will break you and pluck you away

steps.confusionAlert: In the last two lines the גמרא does not write 'God said' or 'David said.' It is still the same back-and-forth: the offer of scholar sons is God's, and the פסוק is דוד's answer.
steps.whatToRemember: In these readings דוד asks that דואג die, and he turns down every offer God makes to soften his punishment: a share in עולם הבא, a teaching said in his name, and scholar sons.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of what is written:
"He will break you and pluck you from the tent,
and uproot you from the land of the living, Selah"?
phrases.notes: תהלים 52:7, the rest of the same פסוק.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Let them say a teaching in the study hall in his name.
He said before Him: "He will break you and pluck you from the tent."
phrases.notes: The 'tent' here is the tent of תורה, so no teaching should be said in his name.

phrases.english: [God said:] Let him have sons who are Torah scholars.
[David answered:] "And uproot you from the land of the living, Selah."

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״יַחְתְּךָ וְיִסָּחֲךָ מֵאֹהֶל וְשֵׁרֶשְׁךָ מֵאֶרֶץ חַיִּים סֶלָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same פסוק and the same dialogue, with smaller offers from God.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד turns down both a teaching quoted in דואג's name and scholar sons for him.

steps.title: דואג's great learning: counting, weighing, and the floating tower
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reads a פסוק in ישעיהו as describing דואג's great learning. He counted every letter of the תורה, weighed every קל וחומר, and listed 300 הלכות about a tower floating in the air.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: What does 'Where is the one who counts, where is the one who weighs, where is the one who counts the towers' mean? 'Where is the one who counts': all the letters of the תורה. 'Where is the one who weighs': he weighed every קל וחומר in the תורה. 'Where is the one who counts the towers': he would count 300 settled הלכות about a tower floating in the air.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק explains three phrases of a פסוק, one by one. Each phrase becomes a picture of how great דואג's learning was, even though it is now lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Counts' means he knew the תורה down to each letter. 'Weighs' means he could work out every קל וחומר. 'Counts the towers' is a play on the word מגדל: he knew 300 הלכות about a strange case, a מגדל floating in the air. The question 'where is he?' shows that all this learning came to nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: קל וחומר arguments (from a lighter case to a stricter one)
a tower (or cupboard) floating in the air

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said: What is the meaning of what is written:
"Where is the one who counts, where is the one who weighs,
where is the one who counts the towers"?
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 33:18

phrases.english: "Where is the one who counts": all the letters in the Torah;
"Where is the one who weighs":
who weighs all the kal vachomer arguments in the Torah;
"Where is the one who counts the towers":

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה סוֹפֵר שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת הֲלָכוֹת פְּסוּקוֹת
phrases.english: who would count three hundred settled halachos
about a tower floating in the air.
phrases.notes: מגדל can mean a tower or a cupboard. The word play is on 'towers' in the פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק, מַאי דִּכְתִיב: ״אַיֵּה סֹפֵר אַיֵּה שֹׁקֵל אַיֵּה סֹפֵר אֶת הַמִּגְדָּלִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from God's dialogue with דוד to a description of how great דואג's learning was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק describes דואג's vast learning: every letter, every קל וחומר, and 300 הלכות about a floating מגדל.

steps.title: Four hundred questions about the floating tower
steps.stepSummary: רבי says that דואג and אחיתופל asked 400 questions about the floating מגדל, and some versions add that not one of them was resolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: דואג and אחיתופל asked 400 questions about a tower floating in the air (and not one of them was answered).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי adds to the picture of דואג's learning. Together with אחיתופל, he asked 400 hard questions about the same floating מגדל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק spoke of 300 settled הלכות. רבי now speaks of 400 open questions, which seems meant to praise how sharp these two were. This sets up רבא's reaction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: אחיתופל, דוד's adviser who turned against him

phrases.english: Rebbi said:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Four hundred questions
Doeg and Achitofel asked
about a tower floating in the air,
(and not one of them was resolved for them).
phrases.notes: Some versions of the גמרא have these words in round brackets and some leave them out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי: אַרְבַּע מְאָה בַּעְיֵי בְּעוֹ דּוֹאֵג וַאֲחִיתוֹפֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another statement about the same floating מגדל from step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דואג and אחיתופל asked 400 questions about the floating מגדל.

steps.title: רבא: asking questions is not greatness
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the idea that asking many hard questions shows greatness. He compares רב יהודה's generation, which learned mainly נזיקין, with his own, which learns a great deal even in עוקצין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is it greatness to ask questions? In the years of רב יהודה, all their learning was in נזיקין, and we learn a great deal in עוקצין!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רבי's statement. Raising hard questions is not, by itself, proof that someone is great.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא gives a comparison from his own world. רב יהודה's generation focused on נזיקין, while רבא's generation studies a lot even in the very hard מסכת עוקצין. Studying hard topics does not make the later generation greater than רב יהודה's. So the 400 questions of דואג and אחיתופל are no real measure of greatness either.

keyTerms.meaning: סדר נזיקין, the order of damages
מסכת עוקצין, a difficult מסכת in סדר טהרות

steps.whyThisMatters: רבא teaches that real greatness is not measured by how sharp or complicated someone's questions are. This fits the whole סוגיא about דואג: great learning without the right inner quality did not save him.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is it greatness to ask questions?
In the years of Rav Yehuda,
all their learning was in Nezikin,
and we learn
a great deal in Uktzin!
phrases.notes: עוקצין is a hard מסכת at the very end of סדר טהרות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the praise implied in רבי's statement about the 400 questions.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the 400 questions show the greatness of דואג and אחיתופל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Raising hard questions is no measure of greatness. A later generation studying hard topics like עוקצין is not greater than רב יהודה's generation, which learned mainly נזיקין.

steps.title: רב יהודה struggled with one משנה in עוקצין
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues his comparison. When רב יהודה reached a certain משנה in עוקצין, he called it as hard as the deep debates of רב and שמואל. Yet רבא's generation learns עוקצין in thirteen academies.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יהודה reached the משנה about a woman pickling vegetables in a pot (some say the משנה about olives pickled with their leaves), he said: 'I see here something as hard as the debates of רב and שמואל!' And we learn עוקצין in thirteen academies!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא keeps building the contrast he started in the last step. He is setting up his big point, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said רב יהודה's generation learned mostly נזיקין. Here רבא adds a vivid example: even a single משנה in עוקצין felt very hard to רב יהודה. By contrast, רבא's generation covers עוקצין in depth, so on the surface they seem to know more.

keyTerms.meaning: מסכת about stems of produce and טומאה, known as very hard
the deep, hard debates of רב and שמואל

phrases.english: And when Rav Yehuda would reach
'A woman who pickles a vegetable in a pot,'
phrases.notes: This is the opening of a משנה in עוקצין.

phrases.english: and some say:
'Olives pickled with their leaves are pure,'
phrases.notes: עוקצין 2:1

phrases.english: he would say: the deep debates of Rav and Shmuel
I see here!
phrases.notes: He means this one משנה felt as hard to him as the toughest debates of his teachers.

phrases.english: And we learn Okatzin
in thirteen academies!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a concrete example to רבא's contrast between the two generations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה found one משנה in עוקצין very hard, while רבא's generation learns עוקצין at length.

steps.title: God wants the heart
steps.stepSummary: Even so, רב יהודה only had to begin taking off his shoes and rain fell, while רבא's generation cries out and is not answered. So הקב״ה wants the heart, as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yet רב יהודה would take off his shoes and rain would come, while we cry out and no one pays attention to us. Rather, הקב״ה wants the heart, as it says: 'And ה׳ looks at the heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the punchline of his comparison. Greatness is measured by the heart, not by how much one learns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The generation that learned less had its prayers answered, and the generation that learned more did not. This proves that many questions and much knowledge are not the real measure. That is exactly why the 400 questions of דואג and אחיתופל do not show greatness.
steps.whatToRemember: Many questions and much knowledge are not the real measure of greatness. הקב״ה wants the heart.

phrases.english: Yet Rav Yehuda would take off his shoes
phrases.notes: Taking off shoes was part of a fast day for rain. Just starting to do it was enough.

phrases.english: and the rain would come,
while we cry out
and there is no one who pays attention to us.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִיבָּא בָּעֵי,
phrases.english: Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, wants the heart,
as it is written: 'And ה׳ looks at the heart.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 16:7

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִיבָּא בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's comparison and draws the lesson from it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The heart, not the amount of learning, is what makes a person great before הקב״ה.

steps.title: דואג and אחיתופל did not understand learning
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא says that דואג and אחיתופל did not really understand their learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: דואג and אחיתופל did not understand the learning.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives his own view of what was wrong with דואג and אחיתופל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב משרשיא seems to explain their unanswered questions by saying they lacked real understanding. This sets up a challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: a piece of learning, a תורה discussion
דוד's adviser who turned against him

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said:
Doeg and Achitofel
did not understand the learning.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new explanation for the failure of דואג and אחיתופל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דואג and אחיתופל lacked real understanding of their learning.

steps.title: מר זוטרא objects from the פסוק about their brilliance
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא challenges this. The פסוק in ישעיהו praises them as counters and weighers, so how can anyone say they did not understand?
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא challenges: these are people about whom it is written 'Where is the one who counts, where is the one who weighs, where is the one who counts the towers,' and you say they did not understand learning?!
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא attacks רב משרשיא's statement using the פסוק we saw earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16 the פסוק was read as describing their huge learning: counting letters, weighing קל וחומר, and the floating tower. People that brilliant cannot be called people who did not understand.

keyTerms.meaning: where is the one who counts

phrases.english: Mar Zutra challenges this:
Those about whom it is written
'Where is the one who counts, where is the one who weighs,
where is the one who counts the towers,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 33:18. This is the same פסוק from step 16.

phrases.english: and you say
they did not understand learning?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב משרשיא's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב משרשיא's claim that דואג and אחיתופל did not understand learning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק in ישעיהו, as read earlier, shows they were brilliant scholars.

steps.title: They understood but never reached the true הלכה
steps.stepSummary: Rather, their learning never led them to the correct הלכה, because God's secret is given only to those who fear Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, their learning did not come out in line with the הלכה, as it says: 'The secret of ה׳ is for those who fear Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא offers his own corrected version of רב משרשיא's statement: their problem was not weak understanding but failing to reach the true הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their minds were sharp, but the right answer in הלכה depends on fear of God. Since they lacked it, all their brilliance never brought them to the truth. This fits רבא's point that the heart is what counts.

keyTerms.meaning: God's secret is for those who fear Him

steps.whatToRemember: Sharp minds without יראת שמים cannot reach the true הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דְּלָא הֲוָה סָלְקָא לְהוּ שְׁמַעְתָּא
phrases.english: Rather, their learning did not come out for them
in line with the halacha,
as it is written: 'The secret of ה׳ is for those who fear Him.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 25:14

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּלָא הֲוָה סָלְקָא לְהוּ שְׁמַעְתָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְהִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: מר זוטרא himself continues with 'אלא' and rephrases רב משרשיא's statement so it fits the פסוק he just cited.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They did not understand learning at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: They understood well but never reached the correct הלכה, because they lacked fear of God.

steps.title: דואג forgot his learning before he died
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says דואג did not die until he forgot all his learning, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: דואג did not die until he forgot his learning, as it says: 'He will die without instruction, and in his great foolishness he will go astray.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to how דואג ended his life. רבי אמי says he lost all his learning first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Without instruction' is read as dying with no learning left. The great scholar ended his life empty of תורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Doeg did not die
until he forgot his learning,
as it is said: 'He will die without instruction,
and in his great foolishness he will go astray.'
phrases.notes: משלי 5:23

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי לֹא מֵת דּוֹאֵג עַד שֶׁשָּׁכַח תַּלְמוּדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the quality of דואג's learning to what happened to him at the end.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דואג forgot all his learning before he died.

steps.title: דואג was struck with צרעת
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says instead that דואג was struck with צרעת, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: he was struck with צרעת, as it says: 'You have destroyed everyone who strays from You.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different account of דואג's end: he became a מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי reads the word הצמתה in the פסוק as hinting at צרעת. He offers a second punishment that befell דואג, alongside רבי אמי's view.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: He was struck with tzaraas,
as it is said: 'You have destroyed everyone who strays from You.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 73:27. רב אשי reads the word for 'destroyed' as a hint to צרעת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different account of what happened to דואג at the end.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דואג was struck with צרעת.

steps.title: How the verse hints at צרעת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how רב אשי's פסוק points to צרעת. It links the word to לצמיתות, whose Aramaic translation לחלוטין recalls a מוחלט, a confirmed מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says there in the תורה, 'לצמיתות' (forever). We translate that word into Aramaic as 'לחלוטין'. And a משנה teaches: the only difference between a quarantined מצורע and a confirmed (מוחלט) one is growing the hair and tearing the clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up רב אשי from the last step. It shows how a word in his פסוק secretly hints at צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word in רב אשי's פסוק sounds like לצמיתות in ויקרא. The Aramaic translation of לצמיתות is לחלוטין, which sounds like מוחלט, the name for a confirmed מצורע. That chain of matching words turns the פסוק into a hint that דואג got צרעת.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarantined מצורע whose signs are not yet clear
Letting the hair grow wild, and tearing the clothes

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה about מוסגר and מוחלט is not being quoted for its law. It is quoted only to show that the word מוחלט means a confirmed מצורע. That one word finishes the chain of word links.

phrases.english: It is written there: "in perpetuity,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:23. This word sounds like the word הצמתה in רב אשי's פסוק.

phrases.english: and we translate it into Aramaic as "lachalutin."
phrases.notes: Listen for the sound: לחלוטין sounds like מוחלט, the word coming up next.

phrases.english: And we learned in a משנה:
There is no difference between a quarantined and a confirmed leper
except letting the hair grow and tearing the clothes.
phrases.notes: This משנה is in מגילה 8b.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק cited by רב אשי in step 25 refers to צרעת.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that דואג was struck with צרעת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A chain of linked words: the word in תהלים, לצמיתות in ויקרא, its Aramaic translation לחלוטין, and the term מוחלט in the משנה in מגילה

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming statements
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן, a list of key words to help remember the order of the statements that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: Three, saw, and half, and called.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line, not an argument. The גמרא gives code words to help you remember the next few statements in order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to one coming statement of רבי יוחנן. 'Three' is the three angels (step 28), 'saw' is 'they did not see each other' (step 29), 'half' is 'they did not live half their days' (step 30), and 'called' is how דוד called אחיתופל (step 32).

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid, a list of code words for the statements that follow

phrases.english: (Mnemonic: Three, saw,
and half, and called)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the צרעת proof to a new set of statements about דואג and אחיתופל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gives memory words for the four statements that follow.

steps.title: Three destroying angels met דואג
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says three angels of destruction met דואג. One made him forget his learning, one burned his soul, and one scattered its ashes in shuls and study halls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Three angels of destruction met דואג. One made him forget his Torah learning. One burned his soul. And one scattered his ashes in the shuls and the study halls.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the first statement of the memory aid, 'three'. He describes three punishments that came upon דואג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This joins together ideas from earlier. Forgetting his learning matches רבי אמי in step 24. רבי יוחנן adds two more punishments: his soul was burned, and its ashes were scattered in places of Torah.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
Three angels of destruction
encountered Doeg:
one who made him forget his learning,
and one who burned his soul,
and one who scattered his ashes
in synagogues and in study halls.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שְׁלֹשָׁה מַלְאֲכֵי חַבָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first statement listed in the memory aid ('three').
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דואג was struck by three angels: one took away his learning, one burned his soul, and one scattered its ashes in places of Torah.

steps.title: דואג and אחיתופל never met
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says דואג and אחיתופל never saw each other. דואג lived in the time of שאול, and אחיתופל lived in the time of דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: דואג and אחיתופל did not see each other. דואג lived in the days of שאול, and אחיתופל lived in the days of דוד.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the second statement of the memory aid, 'saw'. These two wicked scholars, often mentioned together, never actually met.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא keeps naming דואג and אחיתופל side by side, so a learner might picture them together. רבי יוחנן points out that they lived in different times. דואג was in שאול's days, and אחיתופל was in דוד's days.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not see each other

steps.whatToRemember: דואג and אחיתופל are always mentioned together, but they never met. דואג lived under שאול, and אחיתופל lived under דוד.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:

phrases.aramaic: דּוֹאֵג וַאֲחִיתוֹפֶל לֹא רָאוּ זֶה אֶת זֶה.
phrases.english: Doeg and Ahithophel did not see one another.
Doeg was in the days of Saul,
and Ahithophel was in the days of David.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דּוֹאֵג וַאֲחִיתוֹפֶל לֹא רָאוּ זֶה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second statement listed in the memory aid ('saw').
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דואג and אחיתופל never met, because they lived in different times: דואג under שאול and אחיתופל under דוד.

steps.title: דואג and אחיתופל did not live half their days
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that דואג and אחיתופל died before reaching half of their days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: דואג and אחיתופל did not reach half of their days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another statement of רבי יוחנן about these two wicked men: they both died young.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new detail to the list of רבי יוחנן's teachings about דואג and אחיתופל. The point is that their lives were cut short. The next step will bring support for this and give their exact ages.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Doeg and Achitofel did not reach half of their days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another statement by רבי יוחנן in the same series about דואג and אחיתופל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דואג and אחיתופל both died before living half of their days.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports this with a פסוק and their exact ages
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the פסוק that men of blood and deceit will not live half their days, and says דואג lived only 34 years and אחיתופל only 33.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: "Men of blood and deceit shall not live half their days." All of דואג's years were only thirty-four, and אחיתופל's were only thirty-three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי יוחנן, which backs up his statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two things: a פסוק from תהלים saying wicked men do not live half their days, and the actual ages. Both men died in their early thirties. This confirms רבי יוחנן's claim with an older source.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way, in a ברייתא; it introduces support

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
"Men of blood and deceit
shall not live half their days."
phrases.notes: תהלים 55:24

phrases.english: All the years of Doeg
were only thirty-four,
and those of Achitofel
were only thirty-three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's statement in step 30 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that דואג and אחיתופל did not live half their days.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting תהלים 55:24 and giving their ages as 34 and 33.

steps.title: דוד called אחיתופל teacher, then colleague, then student
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says דוד first called אחיתופל his teacher, later his colleague, and in the end his student.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: At first דוד called אחיתופל his teacher, later he called him his colleague, and in the end he called him his student.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a new teaching describing three stages in how דוד spoke about אחיתופל. The next steps will prove each stage from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order goes down step by step: teacher, then equal, then student. This shows אחיתופל's standing in דוד's eyes dropping over time. The גמרא now sets up three proofs, one for each stage.
steps.confusionAlert: The order is not teacher, student, colleague. It goes down one level at a time: teacher, then colleague, then student.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
At first, David called Achitofel his teacher,
and later he called him his colleague,
and in the end he called him his student.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another statement by רבי יוחנן about אחיתופל, this time about his relationship with דוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד's description of אחיתופל went from teacher, to colleague, to student.

steps.title: Proof that דוד first called him teacher
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק where דוד calls אחיתופל "my master" shows that at first he treated him as his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first he called him his teacher, as it says: "But it was you, a man my equal, my master and my familiar friend."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the first stage, that דוד called אחיתופל his teacher, from a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rests on the word אלופי, "my master." Calling someone your master means you see him as your teacher.

phrases.english: At first he called him his teacher:
"But it was you, a man my equal,
my master and my familiar friend."
phrases.notes: תהלים 55:14. The key word is אַלּוּפִי, "my master." That is what shows he was the teacher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the first stage named in step 32.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד first called אחיתופל his teacher.

steps.title: Proof that דוד later called him colleague
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about sharing counsel "together" shows that later דוד treated אחיתופל as an equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Later he called him his colleague, as it says: "That together we would share sweet counsel; in the house of God we walked with the crowd."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second stage, that דוד called אחיתופל his colleague, from the very next פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יחדו, "together," describes two people side by side as equals. So at this stage אחיתופל is no longer above דוד but on the same level.

phrases.english: And later he called him his colleague:
"That together we would share sweet counsel,
in the house of God we walked with the crowd."
phrases.notes: תהלים 55:15. The word "together" is what shows they were equals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the second stage named in step 32.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד later called אחיתופל his colleague.

steps.title: Proof that דוד finally called him student
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the פסוק that shows דוד finally called אחיתופל his student. The פסוק continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the end he called him his student, as it says: "Even my own friend, in whom I trusted..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts the proof for the third stage, that דוד called אחיתופל his student. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the פסוק only describes אחיתופל as a trusted friend. The words that show he was a student come later in the פסוק, which is not finished here.

keyTerms.meaning: my friend, literally "the man of my peace"

phrases.english: And in the end he called him his student:
"Even my own friend,
in whom I trusted,
phrases.notes: תהלים 41:10. The פסוק keeps going right after this, and the proof for "student" comes from its next words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source for the third stage named in step 32.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד in the end called אחיתופל his student.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 41:10, which continues on the next amud.
